name: infinite-menu-loop
summary: An oversized index that never reaches an end: a screenful of items is cloned onto the tail and the scroll position wraps at both edges, so the list reads as endless while every entry stays real markup.

deviations.what: The user-agent regex upstream opens with is replaced by a (pointer: coarse) media query, and a prefers-reduced-motion check is added beside it. Both return the resting state instead of adding a `mobile` class to document.body.
deviations.why: The regex is a 2013-era device table that misses every phone released since, and the thing it protects against is not a device class: writing scrollTop in the middle of a touch fling fights the compositor. A media query states that directly. Touching document.body is also not something a section-scoped effect may do.

deviations.what: The clone count is measured against the menu's own clientHeight rather than window.innerHeight, and the module-scope winsize object is dropped.
deviations.why: Upstream's menu IS the viewport, so the two are the same number there. Here the menu is a column inside a section, and measuring the window would clone far more items than the box can show. Reading a global at module scope is also refused by the effect contract, because it runs at import time.

deviations.what: The upward wrap lands on scrollHeight - clonesHeight - 1 rather than scrollHeight - clonesHeight.
deviations.why: Upstream's two tests meet at exactly the same number. Its downward wrap fires at clonesHeight + scrollPos >= scrollHeight, which is scrollPos >= scrollHeight - clonesHeight -- the position its upward wrap jumps to. Because fitIn is a ceil the equality holds on every layout, not on unlucky ones, so scrolling up off the top bounces straight back to 1 and the menu only loops downwards. Measured in a browser at 8 clones, scrollHeight 2155 and clientHeight 772: the upward target and the downward trigger are both 1355. One pixel inside the boundary is upstream's own idiom -- initScroll parks at 1 rather than 0 for the same reason at the other end -- and with it the menu loops in both directions.

deviations.what: Every clone carries aria-hidden="true" and its links carry tabindex="-1".
deviations.why: A clone is the same link a second time: without this it is a duplicate announcement for a screen reader and a tab stop that leads to a copy of an item the reader already passed.

deviations.what: The requestAnimationFrame handle is kept and cancelled on destroy, the resize listener is removed, the clones are deleted and scrollTop is reset.
deviations.why: Upstream's loop runs for the life of the page because its page never tears the menu down. Here a destroy would otherwise leave a frame loop writing scrollTop into a detached container forever, and a remount would clone the clones.

deviations.what: The menu is a column with a gutter beside it rather than a full-bleed takeover, and overflow-x on the section is clip rather than hidden.
deviations.why: A container that never reaches its own scroll edge never chains wheel events to the page, so a full-bleed loop traps the wheel with no way out. The gutter is ordinary page scroll. `hidden` on the section would compute overflow-y to auto and nest a second scroll container inside the first.
